batch_node.name: aws_core pages v0.4.0
batch_node.description: aws_core's reusable pages (req-aws-core-page-dashboard, -organization, -network): /aws, a dashboard of count tiles, the estate as one picture and two tables; /aws/organization, the OU tree placed by layout tags, with SCP attachments and account placement; /aws/network, transit gateways, attachments, gateways, firewalls and Direct Connect. Every search reads whatever AWS nodes the grid holds: nothing here names a deployment. The children nest under /aws by URL. The graphs share one layout module (aws-estate.js) and the tiles are the aws-counts panel type. v0.2.0 (George, 2026-09-24): the organization graph draws the OU tree only, laid out by aws-organization.js from the nodes' layout:* tags; its scoped, scp and idp searches are gone (on an existing grid, retire those three search nodes: a batch cannot remove a node). v0.3.0 (George, 2026-09-24): the network graph nests each VPC's subnets in it, one column per availability zone, with its internet gateway beside them and a NAT gateway inside its subnet, from PARTITIONED_INTO_SUBNET, ATTACHED_TO_VPC and RESIDES_IN_SUBNET; a subnets table lists each VPC's subnets with zone and CIDR. v0.3.1: the Subnets search drops ORDER BY, which Gryphon refuses on a single-hop traversal (the table sorts client-side). v0.4.0 (George, highbar Q135, 2026-10-02; aws-core-tap#75): /aws/scps lists every SCP, its statements and attachments, with the Deny statements written out as a rulebook (aws-scp-rulebook); /aws/security-groups lists security groups by VPC with rule counts and flags groups open to the internet or allowing every protocol, read from each group's raw rule lists (per-rule nodes are aws-core-tap#64); /aws/baseline is the security baseline per account and region, each control on, off or unknown (aws-baseline); /aws gains an IAM column and /aws/network an exposure column. The SCP attachments panel is mounted on both /aws/organization and /aws/scps.

node.name: AWS counts
node.description: Count tiles over the AWS estate: accounts, OUs, SCPs, VPCs, internet gateways (public front doors and egress exits), internet-facing load balancers, buckets not blocking public access, network firewalls, transit gateways and their attachments, KMS keys, and the accounts inside each compliance boundary. Amber marks a count worth a second look; 'design' marks a count made only of planned nodes.

node.name: AWS
node.description: The AWS dashboard: count tiles over the estate, the estate as one picture (organisation tree, transit gateways and their attachments, VPCs and gateways, boundaries), accounts per OU and what each compliance boundary is scoped from. The organization and network pages go deeper. A column beside them reads IAM: roles by who may assume them (AWS services, other accounts, anyone, or only this account and federation) and the IAM users without MFA.

node.name: What this page can see
node.description: States what the firewall-rules page reads and what it cannot, so a reader does not take a per-group flag for a per-rule finding.

config.text:
Rules are not nodes yet. Each security group carries its rules only in its raw configuration (IpPermissions for inbound, IpPermissionsEgress for outbound), and Gryphon cannot walk into a JSON list.

What this page does with that:
• Rule counts are the length of each list.
• "Open to the internet" and "All-protocol" match the list as text (a CidrIp or CidrIpv6 of 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0; IpProtocol -1). They flag the group when any rule matches. They cannot say whether the open range and the all-protocol entry are the same rule, which ports are open, or what a rule references.
• Outbound 0.0.0.0/0 is AWS's default for every new group, so it is counted, not flagged.

Per-rule nodes, with ports, sources and references as fields and edges, are aws-core-tap#64.
